items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: So he said, 'Would you like to join my group?', so I told him yes... And then myself on drums. Saxaphones were Tab Smith...

ctx.x: And I asked if I could sit in, and they looked at me, because at that time, I only weighed 121 lbs; I was the littlest guy, and I looked like I was about 14 years old.

So they asked me how old I was, so I told them I was 18, but I said I'd be 19 in December --and this was August. So they said, "And you can play?" -- and I said, "I think so." So I got up on the bandstand and I started playing, and everybody started looking around at me, and I played the same thing when I went to Jocks and the same at the Rennie.

items.title: Panama Francis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: A native of Miami, David played his first engagements with the Florida Collegians and in New York with Tab Smith.

ctx.x: Drummer David “Panama” Francis has been performing professionally since the 1930’s. A native of Miami, David played his first engagements with the Florida Collegians and in New York with Tab Smith. Later gigs with Billy Hicks, Roy Eldridge, Lucky Millinder and Cab Calloway made him a familiar and sought-after drummer for both recordings and live shows.
